details: (originally the Vocal division of Federal Screw Works), or just Votrax, was a speech synthesis company located in the Detroit, Michigan area from 1971 to 1996. It began as a division of Federal Screw Works from 1971 to 1973. In 1974, it was given the Votrax name (taken from the name of its first commercial product, the model VS4 "Votrax") and moved to Troy, Michigan and, in 1980, split off of its parent company entirely and became Votrax International, Inc., which produced speech products up until 1984. In 1984, the company restructured itself as a commercial phone/speech audio-response/auto-answering systems company after downsizing some of the staff. In 1987, Votrax merged with Vynet Corp., a voice-recognition prompt pioneer. It remained Votrax inc. until about 1992, when it was renamed to or otherwise merged with Vysion, Inc., a maker of security cameras and other related devices. It remained 'Vysion Inc.' until the company declared bankruptcy in June 1994 following a court battle patent litigation loss against PATCO inc., and from the remains of the old company, restructured itself as 'Maxxar' inc in 1995. explainer.lead: Votrax was a speech synthesis company in the Detroit area active from 1971 to 1996. It matters as an early commercial vendor of speech products, naming itself after its first commercial product.

tiers.eli5: It was a company that made machines which talked, back when that was rare.
tiers.practitioner: Its history illustrates the product lineage of early speech synthesis hardware; modern engineers rarely use it directly, and any pitfall lies in treating legacy synthesis output as representative of current quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Votrax International, Inc. began as the Vocal division of Federal Screw Works (1971–1973), took the Votrax name from its VS4 product in 1974, and split off as Votrax International, Inc. in 1980. No algorithmic details are given.

explainer.example: The company's model VS4 "Votrax" gave the firm its name in 1974.
